text.p: Panama repatriated nearly 100 Colombians, mostly women, children and eldery, who had fled there to escape violence in northwest Colombia, an Interior Ministry spokesman said on Monday.
"The group was returned over the weekend to an unspecified area in Medellin so they will no longer be persecuted," the spokesman said.

The Red Cross gave the refugees food and clothes after they crossed into Panama's Darien jungle from the banana-growing Uraba region in Antioquia where at least four peasants were killed last week by suspected leftist guerrillas.
The area has long been the scene of bitter conflicts between rebels and right-wing paramilitary groups battling for control of lucrative contraband routes.
